title: Financial Sector Reform (Hayne Royal Commission Response No. 3) Bill 2021
short_title: Financial Sector Reform (Hayne Royal Commission Response No. 3) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a financial services compensation scheme of last resort and amend existing laws to support the separate Financial Accountability Regime.
Eligible consumers with unpaid Australian Financial Complaints Authority determinations could apply for compensation of up to $150,000 after recovery steps had failed.
The scheme would cover specified credit activities, personal financial advice and securities dealings, supported by companion bills imposing and collecting industry levies.
changes: A minister-authorised company limited by guarantee would operate the scheme on a not-for-profit basis.
Applicants could not be charged fees for seeking compensation.
The operator would acquire a compensated consumer's recovery rights against a firm in external administration to the extent of the payment.
The Banking Executive Accountability Regime would be repealed as its replacement began applying to banking.
summary.affected: Eligible financial services consumers, financial firms, the scheme operator and financial regulators would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Financial Sector Reform (Hayne Royal Commission Response No. 3) Bill 2021 establishes a compensation scheme of last resort (CSLR) for consumers with unpaid Australian Financial Complaints Authority determinations, capped at $150,000, and makes amendments to support the new Financial Accountability Regime and transitional arrangements from the Banking Executive Accountability Regime.
